subject: Nexera MSA redlines — indemnity, AI-output & cap negotiations
messages:

Date: Fri, 10 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Nexera MSA redlines — indemnity and AI-output protections

Ben —

Attached is our redline of the MSA and Order Form. Two prioritized asks from procurement and legal:

1) Customer right to defend and seek recovery for third-party IP claims (patent/copyright) arising from the service, including any claims tied to model outputs.
2) Explicit indemnity for AI-generated content that allegedly infringes third-party IP or causes loss to our customers — we expect Redwood to defend, indemnify, and hold harmless.

We also propose the liability cap to be equal to 12 months of fees paid under the Order Form and want SOC 2 Type II evidence and a dataflow diagram demonstrating processing of customer prompts/outputs.

Please confirm whether Redwood can accept customer-led defense or whether Redwood insists on defend-and-control. Also indicate whether you will include an AI-output carveout for open-source components and model training data.

Attachments: Nexera_MSA_redline_20260410.pdf

Thanks,
Jane Collins
Contracts Manager — Nexera
contracts@nexera.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: Contracts (Nexera) <contracts@nexera.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Nexera MSA redlines — indemnity and AI-output protections

Jane —

Thanks for the redline and the clear asks. High-level response and proposal:

- Mutuality: Redwood can agree to a third-party IP indemnity tied to use of the Service, but we need mutuality where appropriate (e.g., customer-provided content that causes the claim).

- Defense: Our preference is to defend and control third-party IP claims (standard), with the customer having the right to participate at its own expense. If Redwood cannot assume defense (conflict/coverage issues), we will offer a defined handback process and allow customer to take control with Redwood reimbursement rights for reasonable defense costs.

- AI-output: We propose an AI-output approach that balances customer protection and practical limitations: Redwood will indemnify for third-party IP claims directly resulting from model outputs produced by hosted models under Redwood management. We will propose carveouts for claims attributable to: (a) customer-provided data/prompts that cause the output; (b) open-source model components where indemnity is restricted by upstream license terms; and (c) outputs that arise from illicit prompt engineering (clear bad-faith misuse).

- Cap: instead of a flat 12-month fee cap, we propose a cap tied to committed spend: 3x the monthly committed recurring charge (MRC) at time of claim, with a higher cap available under an enterprise SLA. This scales with usage and aligns with customer risk profile.

I've attached a counter-redline for legal's review (Redwood_counter_redline_20260411.pdf). cc'ing Kim for legal-specific language, and Lauren for commercial fit.

Next steps: Kim — can you review the defense/control language and evidence obligations (SOC2 + dataflow)? Jane — can you share Nexera's expected SLA/commitment numbers so we can compute a concrete numeric cap?

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive — Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com
Attachment: Redwood_counter_redline_20260411.pdf

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, Contracts (Nexera) <contracts@nexera.com>
Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nexera MSA redlines — indemnity and AI-output protections

Ben / Jane / Lauren —

Quick legal note on the counterproposal. I'm attaching a short memo with recommended language and rationales (legal_note_indemnity_20260412.docx). Key points below: 

1) Right to Defend vs. Defend-and-Control: Redwood should keep defend-and-control for efficiency and to preserve access to our vendor relationships (models, infra). Where customer insists, we can provide a narrow option for customer control post-notice if Redwood reasonably refuses or if there is a conflict, provided customer gives Redwood the opportunity to assume defense first. Include clear cooperation and settlement consent clauses (Redwood consent not unreasonably withheld).

2) AI-generated outputs & OSS carveouts: We recommend three carved lines: (i) Redwood indemnifies when outputs are generated by Redwood-hosted models from Redwood-curated model artifacts; (ii) carve-out for outputs directly traceable to customer-supplied content (prompts/data) — customer bears responsibility; (iii) carve-out for third-party open-source components where upstream licenses prohibit indemnity or where vendor terms limit liability.

3) Evidence & mitigation: Add explicit notice windows (30 days for initial notice; 60 days for material claim) and a preservation/evidence checklist. Request sample evidence only (no broad discovery) and prefer secure upload link for artifacts.

4) Cap mechanics: The 3x MRC is a reasonable commercial compromise for mid-market. For enterprise commitments, we can negotiate a higher tier or carve a separate escrow/insurance remedy. Also propose an AI-output-specific subcap where claims solely about generated content are limited to a defined bucket (e.g., 2x MRC) unless willful misconduct is alleged.

I will incorporate these into the attached doc and propose redline language for the defend/control and notice/evidence sections.

Kim Park
Senior Counsel — Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Attachment: legal_note_indemnity_20260412.docx

From: Nexera Counsel <outsidecounsel@nexera-law.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Contracts (Nexera) <contracts@nexera.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Nexera MSA redlines — indemnity and AI-output protections

Kim / Ben —

We appreciate the counterproposals but Nexera cannot accept a broad OSS carveout that effectively strips customer protections. Our position is that the vendor should bear responsibility unless we can show direct causation from a third-party component that was not reasonably disclosed. We will consider a narrow, documented OSS limitation but need stronger disclosure obligations from Redwood (inventory of model components and licensing).

On defense: Nexera requires the right to elect control when Redwood is uninsured for the claim or where Redwood declines to take over within a fixed period. Please include an SLA for Redwood to commence defense (e.g., 30 days after notice) and provide SOC2 Type II report and a redacted model component inventory.

Finally, procurement asks for a one-page summary of how Redwood traces outputs back to model artifacts and any mitigation playbooks for alleged infringement incidents.

Counsel (for Nexera)
outsidecounsel@nexera-law.com

Attachment: none (we will review your legal memo and counter-redline and revert).
